subject: POC Observability Plan — success criteria, dashboards, timelines
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechx.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC Observability Plan — success criteria, dashboards, timelines

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed observability scope for the POC so we can align on success criteria, owners, and a lightweight timeline. Please review and flag anything missing.

High-level POC goal
- Validate Redwood inference integration at scale for your fraud-scoring pipeline with predictable latency and cost.

Observability scope (POC)
- Dashboards: latency P50/P90/P99, token throughput, model error rates (invalid/timeout), request distribution by route/model.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for sample inference requests (request -> model -> response), broken out by service (ingestion, transform, inference, postprocess).
- Logs: structured request/response logs (redacted PII), API error logs, resource-level GPU metrics. We will export logs to your Splunk/Cloud Logging instance.
- Metrics to monitor: token/sec, queue length, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate, model fallback count, cost per 1k tokens.
- Alerts: latency spikes (>P99 threshold), sustained error rate >1%, model fallback >3/min.

Success criteria (provisional)
1) Median latency for 99th percentile load <= 250ms for the primary route.
2) No more than 1% of requests result in 5xx or model timeouts during test window.
3) Ability to export logs/traces to FinTechX stack and populate POC dashboards.
4) Observability dashboards show meaningful baselines within first 48 hours of test.

Proposed owners
- Redwood: implementation of tracing and metric exports, sample dashboards, runbook. (Owner: Marcus Lin)
- FinTechX: ingest dashboards into your observability stack, validate queries, provide test traffic. (Owner: Sam Patel, ENG lead: Liam O'Reilly)

Timeline (rough)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and external contacts — decide retention/PII redaction.
- Week 1: setup tracing integration & log export; deploy sample dashboards.
- Week 2: generate test traffic, iterate on alerts and thresholds.
- Week 3: evaluation window + final readout.

Next steps
- Marcus to share the runbook & sample dashboard (attached).
- Sam — confirm Splunk endpoint and preferred retention for POC logs.
- Jordan — confirm contract milestone for the POC start date.

Attachments: poc-observability-checklist.xlsx, sample-observability-dashboard.png

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan — success criteria, dashboards, timelines

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and in line with what we discussed. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) Splunk details: we'll provide a HEC token and host for log ingestion. Retention for POC logs can be 30 days; we'll confirm exact index names.
2) Tracing: we run Jaeger internally. Is it possible for Redwood to export traces in OTLP/Jaeger format?
3) For success criteria #1: 250ms P99 sounds reasonable, but Liam wants to see both cold-start and steady-state numbers — can you capture cold-start percent of requests that exceed 500ms?

We can commit an initial test window starting Mon Apr 6 (Week 2 in your plan), but we need the tracing/log exports done by Apr 1 to allow ingestion and dashboard build.

Liam — can your team confirm they can generate the sample traffic and the auth details?

Sam

Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan — success criteria, dashboards, timelines

Thanks — confirming the technical plan below.

Tracing:
- Redwood will export spans in OTLP format to your Jaeger collector endpoint. No customer agent required beyond the collector; we will instrument the inference path and sample at adjustable rates.

Logs:
- We'll push structured logs via HTTP to Splunk HEC. We'll provide sample payloads and redaction regex for PII.

Dashboards & Metrics:
- We'll deliver a Grafana JSON model with panels for:
  - Latency (P50/P90/P99) by route/model
  - Cold-start distribution (requests > 500ms)
  - Token throughput and avg batch size
  - KV cache hit rate and model fallback count
  - Cost per 1k tokens and per-route cost breakdown

Alerts:
- Suggested alerts: P99 latency above threshold (configurable), sustained 5xx > 1% over 5m, model fallback >3/min. We'll provide Grafana Alert rules and example Slack webhook config.

Runbook deliverables (will attach in the shared Drive):
- Implementation steps for OTLP/HEC setup
- Dashboard import instructions and example queries
- Test plan for generating synthetic traffic and interpreting results

I'll upload the runbook and the sample dashboard JSON to the Drive folder by EOD Wed Mar 25.

Next steps
- Sam: send HEC token + Jaeger endpoint and confirm index names by Fri Mar 27.
- Marissa/Jordan: sign off on success criteria so we can lock the Apr 6 test window.

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
